description: Canonical source record for the Research section's page content. WordPress is the runtime editor; these files are the recoverable source. Not loaded by WordPress. Block markup in each source file is exactly what the block editor stores in post_content. Approved images are in theme/summit/assets/img/research/; development artwork is held Local-only in its provisional/ folder (git-ignored).

meta.summit_standfirst: Luxury can be priced, described and promoted. Understanding why some objects continue to matter is harder.
meta.summit_intro: Our research examines the objects, decisions and institutions behind lasting luxury — from the published Canon to the wider field studied by The Observatory. It informs our advisory work without becoming an advertisement for it.

meta.summit_summary: The Mystery of Luxury. A book by Gregory Gray and Olivia Dhordain on when an object becomes meaning, and who keeps that meaning alive.
meta.summit_standfirst: At what point does an object stop being merchandise and become something a culture remembers?
meta.summit_intro: Touch Me Not — The Mystery of Luxury, by Gregory Gray and Olivia Dhordain, began with a disagreement about whether that question could be measured. The experiment produced a Canon, a method and a more difficult discovery: the mystery often survives because somebody knows what not to do.

meta.summit_summary: An annual reading of durable luxury objects and the institutions that hold them. The 2027 reading: ninety-nine objects, one empty chair.
meta.summit_standfirst: The Luxury 100 examines objects whose meaning has travelled beyond the moment of purchase. It asks what survives time, institutional change, imitation and commercial pressure.
meta.summit_intro: The original Canon made its case through a declared method. The 2027 annual reading returns to the objects and asks a different question: what has changed — and what has wisely been left alone?

meta.summit_summary: Research carried into a specific question. The New Asian Maison: How Cultural Specificity Becomes Global Luxury.
meta.summit_standfirst: A white paper should be useful before it is impressive. We publish focused studies on the commercial and institutional choices confronting luxury businesses — the evidence, the tensions and the decisions that follow.
meta.summit_intro: Read the argument openly. Where a full paper is available, request a copy through a short form.

meta.summit_summary: Continuing work: the Canon read every year, the field around it, and the questions the method keeps open.
meta.summit_standfirst: Our research programme grows from a simple discipline: ask a question the evidence might answer differently from our first intuition.
meta.summit_intro: Some inquiries extend the Canon and Observatory. Others examine new territory where luxury meets ownership, technology, craft or the client relationship. We publish what the work supports and mark what it cannot yet settle.
